headline: Decision-making is choosing between uncertain futures—a skill you can improve with awareness and structure
universal_truth: Decisions shape destiny; how you choose matters as much as what you choose
fun_facts: The average adult makes about 35,000 decisions per day—most unconsciously
Decision fatigue is real: judges make worse decisions later in the day
Writing out pros and cons activates different brain areas than just thinking about them
discussion_questions: How do you typically make important decisions?
What decisions have you avoided making that are costing you?
How do you handle uncertainty in choices?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Every day, you stand at crossroads—some trivial, some life-changing. What to eat, where to work, who to trust. Decisions shape your future, yet most of us never learned how to make them well. Decision-making is a skill, and skills can be improved.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: We make thousands of decisions daily, mostly on autopilot. But important decisions deserve better. What makes decision-making good or bad?

options.text: Good decisions use relevant information, consider multiple options, account for biases, and match your values—process matters more than luck
options.response: Yes. You can't control outcomes, but you can control process. Good decision-making doesn't guarantee good outcomes—but it improves your odds over time.

options.text: Good decisions are ones that turn out well
options.response: Outcomes involve luck—a good decision can have bad results. What you can control is the process...

q1.title: Process Over Outcome
q1.script: You can make a great decision that leads to a bad outcome (bad luck) or a bad decision that leads to a good outcome (good luck). Judge decisions by the process, not just the result. Over many decisions, good process wins.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Process Over Outcome"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Reversible vs Irreversible
q2.script: Amazon's Jeff Bezos distinguishes reversible decisions (can be undone—decide quickly) from irreversible ones (permanent—decide carefully). Most decisions are more reversible than they feel. Save your deliberation for the truly irreversible.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Write It Out
q3.script: Writing out a decision—options, values, uncertainties—engages your brain differently than thinking alone. Externalize the decision. Make lists. Draw diagrams. Getting it out of your head improves the quality of your thinking.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Decisions shape destiny. How you choose matters as much as what you choose. Invest in your decision-making process.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 184. Tomorrow, we'll explore thinking ahead—planning. Until then, notice a decision you're facing and write out the options.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Decision Writing - Externalize a Choice
growTrack.activity: Take a decision you're currently facing. Write out: What are the options? What matters most to you? What's uncertain? Is it reversible? Externalizing the decision activates different thinking and often reveals the answer.
